items.title: Goa Police defends Oct 11 detention of 7 CJP members in court affidavit, cites 'patronising Umar Khalid'
items.summary: In an affidavit filed before the Bombay High Court on Monday Oct 12 (reported via Bar and Bench ~9:57 AM IST Oct 13), Goa Police justified the Oct 11 detention of seven CJP members at Panaji's Azad Maidan, citing a 'past history' of the outfit violating protest conditions and 'patronising Umar Khalid' — pointing to a July 25 NEET protest where a CJP activist carried 'Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam, Bhima Koregaon' placards and chants of 'Har Ghar me Umar Khalid jalme ga'. The affidavit also alleged a CJP member molested a female officer, denied excessive force, and said the seven were detained at 4:30 PM under BNSS 172(2) for protesting without permission. The HC had ordered their release on Oct 11 (no Sec 163 BNSS order in force) and adjourned the matter to Oct 19.

items.title: Punjab and Haryana HC Bar Association asks members to wear white ribbons in solidarity with advocates 'high-handedly' handled in Delhi
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association asked its members to wear a white ribbon on their coats in solidarity with advocates who it says faced high-handedness in Delhi during the recent protests, per Bar and Bench reporting (13 Oct, 09:11 IST, via protestrecord). Follows the SCAORA Supreme Court plea on illegal detention and manhandling of lawyers during the Oct 10 CEC protest march.

items.title: Police sources claim CJP members entered Jantar Mantar via adjoining JD(U) office premises' boundary wall
items.summary: Maktoob (citing police sources) reported a new police-side detail of Tuesday morning's Jantar Mantar breach: the CJP members allegedly entered the adjoining JD(U) office premises and climbed over its boundary wall to reach the protest site, before Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others were detained. Single-sourced police claim; CJP has not responded to this specific allegation.
